prompt.adult: What animal did Jesus send two disciples to bring, one no one had ever sat on?
prompt.child: Jesus sent two disciples to a village to get an animal no one had ever ridden. What was it?
prompt.teen: Jesus sent two disciples to bring an animal nobody had ever sat on. What was it?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:30, what did Jesus tell the two disciples they would find tied in the village?

verses.text: saying, “Go into the village opposite you, where as you enter you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever sat. Loose it and bring it here.

explanation.adult: Luke 19:30 tells what the disciples would find tied in the village. Read the words after "you will find."
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:30. Find "you will find." The next words name the animal.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:30. The animal is named right after "you will find."
explanation.older: Luke 19:30 names the animal directly after "you will find."

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus told the disciples exactly what they would find, that it would be tied up, and that no one had ever ridden it.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus sent the disciples to bring a colt that no one had ever sat on.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: If anyone asked why they were untying the animal, what were the disciples to say?
prompt.child: If someone asked the disciples why they were untying the animal, what were they supposed to say?
prompt.teen: What were the disciples to say if someone asked why they were untying the animal?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:31, what were the disciples to answer if anyone asked why they were loosing it?

choices.text: The Lord has need of it
We will pay you for it later

verses.text: And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you loosing it?’ thus you shall say to him, ‘Because the Lord has need of it.’ ”

explanation.adult: Luke 19:31 gives the exact words the disciples were to say. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:31. The last words are what the disciples were told to say.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:31. The end of the verse gives the words they should say.
explanation.older: Luke 19:31 closes with the answer Jesus gave them to speak.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus knew the owners would ask. In Luke 19:34 the disciples gave the very answer Jesus told them to give.
teaching.takeaway: The disciples were to say, "The Lord has need of it."

prompt.adult: As Jesus rode along, what did many people spread on the road?
prompt.child: As Jesus rode toward the city, people put something down on the road. What did they spread?
prompt.teen: As Jesus went along, what did many people spread on the road?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:36, what did many spread on the road as Jesus went?

verses.text: And as He went, many spread their clothes on the road.

explanation.adult: Luke 19:36 tells what people put on the road. Read the words after "many spread."
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:36. Find "many spread." The next words tell what they put down.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:36. Right after "many spread" is what they put down.
explanation.older: Luke 19:36 names what was spread on the road, right after "many spread."

teaching.extended_explanation: Spreading something on the road was a way to honor a king. The disciples had already done the same thing for the animal Jesus rode (Luke 19:35).
teaching.takeaway: Many people spread their clothes on the road for Jesus.

prompt.adult: The Pharisees told Jesus to rebuke His disciples. What did Jesus say would happen if the disciples kept silent?
prompt.child: Some Pharisees wanted Jesus to make His disciples stop praising. What did Jesus say would happen if they were quiet?
prompt.teen: Some Pharisees told Jesus to quiet His disciples. What did He say would happen if they stopped?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:40, what did Jesus say would happen if His disciples kept silent?

choices.text: The sky above the city would grow dark
The stones would immediately cry out
The gates of the city would fall down
The birds in the trees would stop singing

verses.text: But He answered and said to them, “I tell you that if these should keep silent, the stones would immediately cry out.”

explanation.adult: Luke 19:40 records Jesus' answer to the Pharisees. Read what He said would happen next.
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:40. Jesus says what would happen if His disciples stopped praising.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:40. Jesus says what would happen if the disciples were quiet.
explanation.older: Luke 19:40 gives Jesus' reply: what would follow if the disciples kept silent.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus meant that praise for Him was so fitting that, if people were quiet, something else would praise instead. Luke 19:40 tells what.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said that if the disciples kept silent, the stones would immediately cry out.

prompt.adult: Jesus had called a man out of his tomb and raised him from the dead. What was the man's name?
prompt.child: Jesus called a man out of a tomb and raised him from the dead. What was his name?
prompt.teen: Whom had Jesus called out of his tomb and raised from the dead?
prompt.older: According to John 12:17, whom had Jesus called out of his tomb and raised from the dead?

verses.text: when He called Lazarus out of his tomb and raised him from the dead

explanation.adult: John 12:17 names the man Jesus had called out of the tomb. Read the name after "called."
explanation.child: Read John 12:17. Find "called." The next word is the man's name.
explanation.teen: Check John 12:17. The man's name comes right after "called."
explanation.older: John 12:17 identifies the man immediately after "called."

teaching.extended_explanation: The people who had been with Jesus that day later told others what they had seen. John 12:17 names the man who came out of the tomb.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus had called Lazarus out of his tomb and raised him from the dead.

review.notes: Sprout stage. Replaced the palm-branches question (gave away the badge name and shared John 12:13 with two other questions). Partial NKJV from John 12:17.

prompt.adult: What was the first word the crowd cried out as Jesus came?
prompt.child: When the crowd met Jesus, they shouted. What was the first word they shouted?
prompt.teen: What was the first word the crowd shouted when they met Jesus?
prompt.older: According to John 12:13, what was the first word the crowd cried out when they met Jesus?

explanation.adult: John 12:13 records what the crowd cried out. Read the first word inside the quotation marks.
explanation.child: Read John 12:13. Find what the crowd shouted. Look at the first word in quotation marks.
explanation.teen: Check John 12:13. The first word of the shout comes right after "cried out."
explanation.older: John 12:13 quotes the crowd; the first word follows "cried out."

teaching.extended_explanation: The crowd's shout is a word of praise that once meant "save us." It is the first word in the quotation in John 12:13.

prompt.adult: Why did the people also meet Jesus as He came?
prompt.child: Why did the people go out to meet Jesus?
prompt.teen: For what reason did the people also meet Jesus?
prompt.older: According to John 12:18, why did the people also meet Jesus?

choices.text: Because they wanted to watch a great parade go by
Because the leaders told them they had to go
Because they heard that He had done this sign
Because they hoped He would give them bread and fish

verses.text: For this reason the people also met Him, because they heard that He had done this sign.

explanation.adult: John 12:18 gives the reason the people met Him. Read the words after "because."
explanation.child: Read John 12:18. Find the word "because." The rest of the verse tells why.
explanation.teen: Check John 12:18. The reason comes right after "because."
explanation.older: John 12:18 states the reason immediately after "because."

teaching.extended_explanation: The crowd came out because of something they had heard Jesus do. John 12:18 names that reason.
teaching.takeaway: The people met Jesus because they heard that He had done this sign.

prompt.adult: The Pharisees said among themselves that something had gone after Jesus. What?
prompt.child: The Pharisees saw how many people were following Jesus. What did they say had gone after Him?
prompt.teen: The Pharisees complained that something had gone after Jesus. What was it?
prompt.older: According to John 12:19, what did the Pharisees say had gone after Jesus?

verses.text: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, “You see that you are accomplishing nothing. Look, the world has gone after Him!”

explanation.adult: John 12:19 records the Pharisees' words. Read the last sentence of the verse.
explanation.child: Read John 12:19. The Pharisees' last sentence says what had gone after Jesus.
explanation.teen: Check John 12:19. The last sentence tells what they said had gone after Him.
explanation.older: John 12:19 ends with the Pharisees' complaint about who had gone after Him.

teaching.extended_explanation: The Pharisees felt they could not stop the crowds. In John 12:19 they exaggerated to say how many people were following Jesus.
teaching.takeaway: The Pharisees said, "The world has gone after Him!"
